requirements.title: Part 1: Setup
requirements.description: Create a marimo notebook and use the supplied sentiment lexicons. Small language models are optional.
criteria: Required sentiment lexicon data is available; missing instructor resources are an environment blocker, not proof of incomplete student work.

requirements.title: Part 2: Find a work of fiction
requirements.description: Select long-form fiction of at least 15,000 words, excluding A Christmas Carol. Non-English work needs its own lexicon and English translations.
criteria: Identify the selected work and establish that it is eligible fiction, not A Christmas Carol.
Verify at least 15,000 words in the text actually analyzed (raw attachment counts are only supporting evidence).
For non-English work, review the supplied lexicon and English translations.

requirements.title: Part 3: Make predictions
requirements.description: Written predictions and reasoning before examining results. Source order cannot prove chronology.
criteria: Predictions address ranking positive versus negative passages.
Predictions discuss whether sentiment fits a single positive/negative axis.
Reasons are supplied; timing requires human review.

requirements.title: Part 4: Display sentiment arcs
requirements.description: Load and segment the document, apply basic lexicon-based sentiment analysis, display results using at least two methods, and discuss effectiveness and differences.
criteria: Document loading and segmentation are implemented.
Results from at least two methods are displayed; inspect actual outputs.
Written observations discuss effectiveness and differences.

requirements.title: Part 5: Rank passages
requirements.description: Sort passages by sentiment; inspect high, low and middle passages; discuss the evidence used, its effectiveness and differences.
criteria: High, low AND middle passages are inspected.
Written discussion addresses what evidence methods use, its effectiveness and differences.

requirements.title: Part 6: Discuss
requirements.description: Reflect on the process: challenges, what worked well, and what did not.
criteria: What did not work well is discussed.
